source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Increase fiber gradually, drink adequate fluids as appropriate, stay active, and respond to the urge to have a bowel movement during the day.","B":"Restrict fluid intake, decrease dietary fiber, and delay bowel movements when inconvenient so the colon can adapt to less frequent elimination.","C":"Use a stimulant laxative every day as the first prevention strategy, even when diet, fluids, activity, and bowel habits have not been addressed.","D":"Avoid regular physical activity and reduce fruit and vegetable intake because both can increase intestinal motility and worsen constipation."}}
source_row.rationale: NIDDK recommends adequate fiber, sufficient fluids, regular physical activity, and healthy bowel habits for constipation prevention and management. Option A is correct. Option B reduces both fluid and fiber intake and encourages delaying defecation, all of which work against prevention. Option C makes a daily stimulant laxative the first strategy before basic measures have been addressed. Option D removes physical activity and reduces fiber-rich produce even though those measures can support bowel function.
source_row.source_detail: NIDDK — Treatment for Constipation: increase fiber, drink adequate liquids when appropriate, engage in regular physical activity, and establish healthy bowel habits/respond to the urge to defecate; stimulant laxatives are not the default first prevention measure. Current NIDDK constipation guidance at cited federal URL; live content rechecked 2026-08-15.
